answer: A durable defense is stake-weighted reputation: every agent must lock collateral before it can transact, and each completed job adds a verifiable attestation to its record. A Sybil attacker who spawns a grove of fake identities must fund each one, so forging a thousand reputations costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents wander freely through the network, earning trust once and reusing it everywhere. Slashing burns the stake of any identity caught misbehaving, turning the attacker's voyage into a losing trade: fakes cost more to maintain than they ever earn.
